Uniejow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Uniejów, Poland

Demolished. Uniejów, granted town rights in 1285, saw Jewish settlement from the mid-18th century, with an independent kehilla established in the mid-19th; population reached 1,400 (40%) by 1939. A 1940 ghetto held about 130 families; after liquidation, most were murdered at Chełmno. This cemetery, likely established in the 19th century, received its last known burial in 1941 before Germans completely destroyed it. A 1965 application formally requested its closure. Not a single tombstone survives; only a memorial plaque reading 'The Jewish cemetery. Legally protected area. Please, respect the resting place of the dead' marks the site, its original 69-acre area now reduced to 49.
